title: Trig Identities and Equations
subtitle: The other four trig functions, the identities worth knowing, and solving trig equations.

questions.explain: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine.
A 2 inside the function does not come out. The true identity is $sin(2x) = 2sin(x)cos(x)$.
Going clockwise instead flips the height: sine is an odd function.
Going clockwise instead leaves the $x$-coordinate alone: cosine is an even function.
$sin^(-1)(x)$ is the inverse function, arcsine. $frac{1}{sin(x)}$ is $csc(x)$.
$tan = frac{sin}{cos}$, and you cannot divide by 0. That is where the graph of tangent has its vertical asymptotes.

questions.explain: Here $sin = frac{1}{2}$ and $cos = frac{sqrt(3)}{2}$, so $tan(frac{pi}{6}) = frac{sqrt(3)}{3}$.

questions.explain: Here $sin = frac{sqrt(2)}{2}$ and $cos = frac{sqrt(2)}{2}$, so $sec(frac{pi}{4}) = sqrt(2)$.

slides.text: The other four trig functions are all built from sine and cosine. Match each one.
slides.hint: Secant goes with cosine, cosecant goes with sine. Each pair has exactly one "co".
slides.explain: So if you know sine and cosine on the unit circle, you know all six.

slides.text:
For example:$$tan(frac{pi}{4}) = frac{sin(frac{pi}{4})}{cos(frac{pi}{4})}$$
At $frac{pi}{4}$, sine and cosine are both $frac{sqrt2}{2}$. So what is $tan(frac{pi}{4})$?

slides.text:
The point $(cos(theta), sin(theta))$ is on a circle of radius 1, so the Pythagorean theorem gives the most-used identity of all:$$sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1$$
If $sin(theta) = frac{3}{5}$ and $theta$ is in the first quadrant, what is $cos(theta)$?
slides.explain: $cos^2(theta) = frac{16}{25}$, and cosine is positive in the first quadrant, so $cos(theta) = frac{4}{5}$.

slides.text: Solving a trig equation means finding points on the circle. Tap **every** angle from 0 to $2pi$ where $sin(theta) = frac{1}{2}$.
slides.hint: Sine is the height of the point. Which points are at height $frac{1}{2}$?
slides.explain: Two answers: $frac{pi}{6}$ and $frac{5pi}{6}$. A trig equation almost always has more than one solution.
